claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a single-phase high-temperature BCC alloy.
Lower temperatures create a thermodynamic driving force for chemically ordered, B2-like clustering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Sluggish atomic diffusion kinetically retards ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
High configurational entropy and rapid thermal agitation suppress ordering and stabilize the high-temperature BCC phase.
Decreasing temperature or extending annealing time allows the tendency toward chemical decomposition to overcome kinetic barriers.
Ordering or decomposition produces a two-phase B2+BCC microstructure.
Changing annealing time and cooling rate changes the time available for atomic diffusion.
Atomic diffusion is moderate in the proposed intermediate annealing-temperature regime.
Short-range chemical order or incipient B2-like clusters emerge within the BCC matrix during suitable thermal treatment.
Decreasing configurational entropy and increasing chemical-potential differences favor ordering and decomposition.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing will nucleate and grow B2 precipitates in the BCC matrix.
Rapid quenching will kinetically retain a single-phase high-temperature BCC structure.
A rapidly cooled as-synthesized baseline will have minimal detectable ordering.
Ordering becomes important below a critical temperature only when atomic mobility remains sufficient for ordering to begin.
Extreme overaging or very high temperatures may produce additional transformations outside the proposed mechanism.
The mechanism would be falsified if slow-annealed and rapidly quenched samples consistently exhibited the same phase composition despite different diffusion times.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe a high-temperature BCC stability regime, whereas the boundary describes the BCC phase at sufficiently high temperature as metastable; stable and metastable are not equivalent thermodynamic states.
